text:
You need a way to set a custom homepage for the Google Chrome app on iPad devices through Jamf and deploy it across your iPad fleet.

I’d be glad to help with that. I’m Tobias Reyne, and I have 7 years of experience building web and full stack solutions with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. While your request is more about deployment and browser behavior than building a large app, I’m comfortable working in the kind of implementation details that make these setups reliable and easy to roll out.

One relevant project I can share is a clipboard sync browser extension for Clipboardly, a productivity software client. I built a Chrome extension that syncs saved snippets across devices through a small Express API using TypeScript, the Chrome Extensions API, Express, and MongoDB. That project reached 9k weekly active users and maintained a 4.7 store rating. It gave me practical experience working with Chrome extension behavior and cross-device user workflows, which is useful when configuring a managed Chrome experience through Jamf.

For your use case, I’d focus on understanding exactly how the Chrome app is managed on iPad in your environment, then configuring the homepage behavior so it opens the correct URL consistently for your fleet. If needed, I can help verify the setup, test it on a device, and make sure the deployment approach is straightforward for your team to maintain.

Since you only expect 1–2 hours of work, I’d aim to keep the scope tight: confirm the target URL, review the Jamf configuration path you’re using, implement the homepage setup, and validate that it deploys cleanly to the iPad devices.

What Jamf setup are you currently using for the Chrome app on iPad, and do you already have the homepage URL you want deployed?
